Transgenic Nicotianabenthamiana plants expressing grapevine fanleaf virus (GFLV), a nepovirus, coat protein were protected against GFLV infection.
transgenic tobacco plants expressing the grapevine fanleaf virus coat protein are partially protected against infection by virions or viral RNAs.
transgenic plants expressing the coat proteins of nepoviruses can be protected against virus infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of transgenic plants resistant to virus infection.
the development of a transgenic strategy to protect grapevines against GFLV.
the expression of the coat protein (CP) of the Grapevine fanleaf nepovi- rus (GFLV, genus Nepovirus) in transgenic tobacco (Nicotiana benthami- ana) plants.

the coat protein gene of GFLV can be used as a gene of interest for engineering transgenic plants with resistance against GFLV.
the coat protein of GFLV is involved in the systemic invasion of the host plant and is therefore a potential target for the development of virus-resistant transgenic plants.
coat protein expression in transgenic plants is able to provide partial resistance against GFLV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coat protein of GFLV is involved in the systemic invasion of plants.
the coat protein of GFLV has the potential for use as a transgenic control of the “court-nouè” disease.
the coat protein of GFLV is a determinant of resistance to GFLV infection in transgenic plants.

transgenic expression of a viral coat protein can provide some degree of protection to a virus infection.
